about: Hand-authored input of tools/anim_graph/export_actor_b_graph.py. It maps Frontier roles to graph states/leaves, names the overlay selections, and labels every runtime transition rule. Graph values (records, fades, gates) are copied by the exporter from player_blending.json; this file never restates them except in 'expect' blocks that the exporter asserts. Fidelity policy: the graph's authored behaviour is the default; every gameplay deviation is an opt-in flag in gameplay_overrides. One overlay loop (resolver_policy) resolves every leaf; a resolver_choices entry may use the other loop only to keep a behaviour Frontier has today (basis frontier_requirement), and the graph result is exported beside it.

spear.why: thrown weapon (throwables_design.md 3.4; THROW2: carried overhand above the shoulder, carry_overrides): the graph's pick-up weapon base (one-handed throw aim tree, 1h carry arm, brick-fingers grip, throw-object-* chain) with the brick sub-type (the sub-type whose fingers are the base's own; its records only point the aim-run pitch additives and the quick throw at the aimed throw clips). Draw-holster long-gun: the spare spear is slung on the back and the long-gun draw ends with it in the right, throwing hand (loadout_design.md 5.2, spear pair @ long_A)

tomahawk.why: thrown weapon: pick-up weapon base with the brick sub-type (see spear). Draw-holster grenade, the graph's set for thrown objects: it has no records, so the draw falls through to actor_b's own one-handed draw (stealth-draw-p^idle--arm-r, from the right hip / belt), on which weapon-base-pick-up lays its brick-fingers layer (records 0x00012e30 / 0x00012e44). THROW2: carried like a hatchet (carry_overrides) and drawn from the back of the belt with the graph's thrown-object draw (action_overrides)

atlatl.why: thrown weapon (dart cast from the spear-thrower): as the tomahawk; the next dart is fitted with the bow's nock reach (pinned_actions)

order: 2. that role's layers, in listed order (ascending overlay priority, then record offset; INFERRED), including move-set finger layers such as actor_b-p-sprint-fingers / actor_b-fist-caut-hands

3. weapon partial slot: the weapon-out finger state (weapon_layers.weapon_out; musket and pistol, see apply_rule) while no action plays; an action's partial (actions.*.partial: draw, holster, grab, nock, reload) replaces it in the same slot
4. weapon additive slot: the action's twin (actions.*.twin)

weapon_out.weight_source: INFERRED: idle-pistol-out-part is a code-entered partial state with no weight in the data; played at 1
weapon_out.applies_to: lower-body roles (roles.*, runtime_roles.hit_full/death) whenever a weapon is out, as a looping partial after all of the role's layers (step 3 of order), for the weapons it applies to (weapon_out.clips[*].applies). It is faded out by the aim weight: aim_trees carry their own hands layer (aim_trees.<w>/<s>.hands), which a full-weight weapon-out partial would hide (INFERRED).
weapon_out.apply_rule_why: The partial applies to a weapon only when that weapon's weapon-base set remaps the state's leaf 1p-idle-fingers (long-gun 0x00009cac, pistol 0x00019368). weapon-base-bow has no such record: the leaf falls through to actor_b's generic actor_b-p-hands (0x00000328), and the bow's fingers come from its state-keyed actor_b-p-bow-hands layers on the locomotion states, which a full-weight generic partial played after them would hide. Order, weight and trigger stay INFERRED; WP5 should confirm the bow from screenshots and can set force.bow.

notes: idle-pistol-out-part (reference clip 1p-idle-fingers) has no incoming transition record: the game code enters it. It is the only looping state of the weapon partial group; idle-hands is its no-weapon counterpart. That it plays whenever a weapon is out is INFERRED from the state name and structure.
pistol: weapon_out resolves to actor_b-r-hand-revolver, the only clip that keys r_hand_prop_attachment on pistol locomotion (r-arm-gun keys 6 arm bones, sprint-fingers keys no prop bone).

musket: weapon_out resolves to actor_b-p-rifle-idle-hands (Godot action actor_b-p-rifle-crouch-idle--hands) standing. In crouch the export loop (asc_once) disables it (actor_b 0x00003974 -> null); the asc_fix result is used there by bindings.resolver_choices (user requirement 2, see meta.resolver_exceptions).

bow: not applied (apply_rule). The leaf would resolve to the generic actor_b-p-hands (Godot action actor_b-fist-caut-hands), which keys palm and finger bones but no prop bone and would override the authored state-keyed actor_b-p-bow-hands finger pose on every bow lower-body role.

prop_bones_source: tests/check_weapon_axes.gd hand_bone (the prop bone each Frontier weapon is attached to)

prop_exempt.roles.*/*/hit_full: direct role: the clip is supplied at runtime; checked on runtime_roles.hit_full
prop_exempt.roles.*/*/hit_add: direct additive role: applied over another role, which drives the prop bone
prop_exempt.roles.bow/*/death: death-front-mid carries no bow layer and the weapon-out finger partial does not apply to the bow (weapon_layers.weapon_out; its generic clip would key no prop bone anyway), so nothing in the graph drives l_hand_prop_attachment during death; the runtime decides whether the bow stays attached (Frontier has no death today)
prop_exempt.roles.bow/*/land_death: as roles.bow/*/death: fall-land-death (land-hard-damage^death) carries no bow layer; Frontier has no fall damage, so the landing rule never selects it
prop_exempt.runtime_roles.death.bow/*/*: as roles.bow/*/death: the runtime death clips carry no bow layer
prop_exempt.roles.spear/*/*: thrown weapon: the throw clips key no prop bone (throwables_design.md 3.3) and Throwable._place_held places the held object itself after every skeleton update; the prop bone only carries the socket (the brick-fingers layer poses it)

resolver_policy.why: One overlay loop for every leaf. The engine's loop is not in the data, but the authored records only make sense under asc_once (restart from the lowest-priority layer after every hit): under asc_fix the whole crouch bow-draw family is dead, and asc_once treats the long-gun weapon-out arms in crouch the same way whether they are reached as a layer target or as a substitution. The two loops give the same result on every other exported leaf and layer target.
evidence: crouch-crouch 0x0001ba58 (tense-bow-draw -> crouch-bow-draw) and 0x0001ba6c (#1966cf23 -> #e4be6359), and actor_b 0x00003e60 / 0x00003e74 (-> actor_b-p-crouch-bow-reload--part / --add): under asc_fix no state leaf and no layer target reaches them in any of the 12 weapon x mode selections, because tense-bow-draw / #1966cf23 exist only as weapon-base-bow outputs (0x00004df8 / 0x00004de4) and actor_b (priority 37) consumes them in the same ascending pass before crouch (priority 9) is revisited. Under asc_once they are live exactly for the bow's crouch reload (tests/test_export.py test_resolver_policy_evidence).

idle-gunout-1lg2h-arms in crouch: as a layer target (weapon-base-long-gun flags 01 records such as 0x0000a508) it resolves through crouch 0x0001b9e0 and actor_b 0x00003974 to null under both loops; only asc_once gives the same null when it is reached from 1p-idle-fingers (weapon-base-long-gun 0x00009cac), while asc_fix lets actor_b 0x000039b0 consume it first (actor_b-p-rifle-idle-hands).

hand_states.musket/crouch.weapon_out.requirement: user requirement 2: weapons stay attached to the hand prop bones and placed by the game's --hands / carry --arms clips
hand_states.musket/crouch.weapon_out.why: Not a claim about the game's loop. Under the export loop (asc_once) this leaf follows crouch 0x0001b9e0 into actor_b 0x00003974 (-> null), which disables the musket's weapon-out finger partial in crouch. Nothing then drives r_hand_prop_attachment at full weight in most musket crouch roles (crouch locomotion at 0.8 from rifle-crouch-run-arms; idle turns, takeoff, jump, several landings and death at 0; the export counts them in meta.resolver_exceptions). Measured in Godot 4.7, the rifle grip keys (rifle-crouch-run-arms, rifle-crouch-idle--hands) put that bone 4.2 cm and 36 deg from its rest pose, so the musket would visibly twist in the hand. To keep today's behaviour this one leaf uses the asc_fix result actor_b-p-rifle-idle-hands (Godot action actor_b-p-rifle-crouch-idle--hands). The graph result (null) is kept in resolver_alternatives; set enabled to false to export it, and (g) then exempts the listed roles.

crouch_change.why_substitute: crouch-change-idle^idle resolves to stand^crouch / crouch^stand, which have no Actor_B action. Actor_B has the unreferenced full-body pair actor_b-p-stand^crouch--base / actor_b-p-crouch^stand--base (same 1.0 s timing as the graph-resolved weapon additives; '--base' names the base of the stand^crouch--add family). They play in place of the missing clip while options.crouch_change_full_body is on (the default, graph-faithful path); status stays 'substitute'.

pinned_actions.about: Frontier action keys the graph has no state for, pinned to a resolved graph action (copied with its records and asset ids; status frontier_pinned). Throwable.action_started('draw', draw_time) takes the next weapon after a throw; a thrown object in the source game is not replaced, so no graph state takes the next one.

spear/stand/draw.why: the next spear comes off the back: the profile's own draw (long-gun draw, right hand)

tomahawk/stand/draw.why: the next tomahawk comes off the belt: the profile's own draw

atlatl/stand/draw.why: the next dart comes off the belt: the profile's own draw (as the tomahawk), with the board kept in the right hand. Not the bow's nock reach (bow/stand/nock, throwables_design.md 3.4): its r_hand_prop_attachment keys carry the bow's arrow from the right hand to the bow hand, and on the atlatl that bone holds the board, which then left the right hand for the left (up to 0.65 m off both palms, 0.57 s in the left hand; THROW review)

action_overrides.about: THROW2 (user playtest 2026-09-25): graph action states whose clips Frontier substitutes (status frontier_substitute). The state, its records and callbacks (start phase, rate) stay the graph's; the substitute clips are given by graph name and resolved through the actor_b overlay like any leaf, with the overlay records as evidence; the replaced clips stay in `replaced`. Pinned rows (pinned_actions) copy the substituted row.

tomahawk/stand/equip.why: the tomahawk is drawn from the back of the belt, where the loadout carries it (loadout_design.md: back.tomahawk, head on the belt; handoff_survey.md 6: the graph's one-hand thrown-object draw molotov-pack-draw starts with the right hand at the small of the back, 2.1 cm from the carry point), not with the pistol draw from behind the right hip (stealth-draw-p^idle--arm-r, the grenade draw-holster set's fall-through)

tomahawk/crouch/equip.why: as tomahawk/stand/equip (no crouched variant; the pistol draw was the same clip crouched)

tomahawk/stand/holster.why: the graph's holster plays the draw clip backwards (start phase 1, negative rate): the tomahawk goes back to the small of the back

tomahawk/stand/holster_finish.why: the empty hand back from the small of the back: the draw clip forward from the held holster frame, as the stand pistol's finish resolves to its draw clip (the molotov set has no stow)

tomahawk/stand/grab.why: draw step 1, the hand from idle to the tomahawk at the small of the back (the thrown-object put-away reach, idle^draw; handoff_survey.md 6)

throw.about: The graph's aimed throw chain for the thrown-weapon profiles (throwables_design.md 3.2): aim-idle / aim-run -> (throw-object-aim, the 0.2 s raise, from aim-run) -> throw-object-aim-start (release-start, 0.2 s) -> auto at phase 1, fade 0 -> throw-object-aim-end (release-end, 0.6 s) -> at phase 0.8 throw-object-aim^idle (back to carry) or throw-object-aim^aim (back to aim; no Actor_B clip), with the movement / crouch exits of both. Each state has one leaf, resolved per profile and stance like the other roles.

missing_notes.recover_aim: 1h-aim-throw-release-end^aim has no Actor_B clip (throwables_design.md 3.2); the runtime crossfades from release-end into the aim tree over the graph's 0.2 s (transitions throw_end_to_aim) in its place

release.source: tests/throwables/survey_throw_clips.gd: the right hand is fastest (10.2-11.5 m/s standing, 8.8 crouched) in release-end's first key interval; the object leaves 0.05 s into release-end at 1x (0.25 s into the 0.8 s start + end chain, Throwable.RELEASE_PHASE). The graph has no release event state (its +0x2c callback i32[D0+156] is a per-state runtime integer), so the game supplies it: PlayerAnim calls Throwable.release_from_animation()

carry_overrides.about: THROW2 (user playtest 2026-09-25): carries of thrown weapons the user wants held unlike the graph's pick-up weapon base (its 1h carry arm, p-1h-arm--part, holds an object up in front of the chest). A row replaces the weapon-base layers of its `replace` slots on every lower-body role of its modes that carries such a layer (idle, direction banks, starts, stops, reversals, turns; air, landing, hit and death roles carry no weapon-base arm layer), except `roles_except` (and, when given, only `roles_only`), with (1) `from_profile`: the weapon-base layers of those slots that another graph profile resolves on the same role (its records and lambda weights; a target with no Actor_B action takes `substitute`, a role that profile has no record on takes its idle role's), then (2) `poses`: [pose, weight] pairs, each an Actor_B clip sampled at one key time (`sample_s`) on a bone mask, baked by TreeBuilder (the clip's asset ids and attribution are kept). Rows apply in order; a later row replaces an earlier row's layers. Layer status: 'frontier' (pose), 'substitute', 'resolved' (the other profile's graph layer); every role lists its rows in `carry_override` with the layers they replaced. Unchanged: the throw chain, the aim trees and their grips (the wound-up pose, release and follow-through), and the draws (action_overrides changes the tomahawk's).

javelin_carry.why: the overhand javelin carry the user asked for ('they should kind of hold it above the shoulder'): the graph's throw raise (throw-object-aim, leaf 1h-aim-throw-aim) at its middle key (0.1 s of 0.2 s, an authored key), the right arm chain only, over the locomotion's torso: the hand above and just in front of the shoulder, the elbow out at shoulder height; the carry-to-wind-up transition is the aim tree coming in at Weapon.aim over it

javelin_carry_crouch.why: crouched: the raise's last key (the cocked arm of the throw aim). On the crouch clips' forward-bent torso the middle key puts the hand in front of the chest, the last key beside the face with the elbow up; the crouched throw clips cock the hand low behind the hip (1h-aim-crouch-throw-idle), so the standing raise is used

knife_ready_arm.source_state: knife ready pose (melee_prone.md 2.3: hit1-intro start = hit1 end = hit3 end)
knife_ready_arm.why: Actor_B's knife ready pose (the first frame of the knife chain) on the arm at a relaxed weight over the machete carry arm (knife--arm): it turns the thumb up, so the haft stands up out of the fist (head up, blade forward) with the upper arm at the side; with the carry arm alone the haft points forward like a pistol barrel (user playtest)

melee_guard_arm.source_state: melee-tell (the graph's melee guard layer; melee_prone.md 3.1: guard actor_b-p-melee-tell-idle--arms)
melee_guard_arm.why: crouched: Actor_B's melee guard arm (the right arm of the melee-tell pose). On the crouch clips' forward-bent torso the knife ready arm lays the haft forward along the ground (7-25 degrees up); the guard arm holds it up and forward, the fist low in front (crouched idle: the haft about 44 degrees up; crouch walking it leans on to 19-25 degrees, so the moving roles add melee_guard_crouch_fw_arm)

melee_guard_crouch_fw_arm.source_state: melee-tell, crouched and moving (the actor_b overlay remaps crouch-melee-tell-walk-fw--arms and crouch-melee-tell-walk-bw--arms to this clip)
melee_guard_crouch_fw_arm.why: crouched and moving: the graph's crouch-walk melee guard arm at half weight over melee_guard_arm. Alone it raises the fist to the chest (the guard before a strike); at 0.5 the haft stands about 40-46 degrees up on the crouch walk's forward-bent torso with the fist 0.25 m below the shoulder, as crouched idle (probe, crouch walk)

knife_grip.why: saber_model.md 3.5 option 1: the fingers, palm and prop bone of the first frame of atk-actor_b-knife-v-thug-hit1-intro (the knife ready pose) as the carry grip layer instead of p-knife--fingers, which keys the prop bone 146 degrees off the attack clips; the fist closes round the haft, which runs along prop +Y (the finger channel) with the edge on the finger side (prop -Z)

spear.why: overhand javelin carry (user playtest 2026-09-25), relaxed weight 0.9 over the locomotion arm (Godot's rest-relative blend of a partial layer below weight 1 lowers the raised arm more than a slerp: at 0.8 the running hand fell below the shoulder in game): the hand at about shoulder height and above it, the elbow up; the spear is held level, point forward (Throwable.carry_rot_deg)

the sprint mode's idle is the walk / run idle input (one idle input per weapon): the same javelin carry. The sprint's moving roles (starts, the direction bank, stops, reversals) keep the pick-up base's own sprint arm (p-1h-arm--part at the graph's records and weights): sprinting lowers the spear to a port carry in front of the body (Throwable.carry_low_rot_deg turns it point up and across as the hand drops), and the sprint-to-run mode fade raises it again. THROW2 review: the machete sprint arm's trail at the side (knife--arm 0.6, the first THROW2 build) swings the fist within 3-4 cm of the hip joint, where no spear orientation through the fist clears the thigh by more than 2 cm (throwables_design.md 6.1)

tomahawk.why: carried like a hatchet, one-hand melee carry (user playtest 2026-09-25: 'held like a pistol'): the graph's one-hand melee carry arm (weapon-base-machete: every machete-arm-* is actor_b-p-knife--arm for Actor_B, records 0x00016380 idle 0.7 / 0x00016448, 0x00016434 moving 0.6 and the start / stop / reversal records at 0.6; Actor_B has no clip for the relaxed idle / walk / run arms, so those take knife--arm, the same carry arm; the turns have no machete record and take the idle's), then the knife ready arm at 0.6

sprinting: the knife ready arm at full weight over the machete sprint arm (knife--arm 0.6), so the haft stays up out of the pumping fist; the idle keeps the carry of walk / run (one idle input for walk / run / sprint)

crouched: the machete crouch arm (knife--arm, records as walk / run) under the knife ready arm (0.6, as standing) and the melee guard arm (melee_guard_arm) at 0.6. THROW2 review: the guard arm at full weight held the tomahawk head at the mouth (8 cm from the chin); at 0.6 over the ready arm the head stays 0.25 m from the face with the haft 25-29 deg up and the blade forward
the knife grip (knife_grip) in place of the brick fingers on every lower-body role: the fist round the haft

crouched and moving (every crouch role but the idle and the idle turns, which keep the row above): the graph's crouch-walk melee guard (melee_guard_crouch_fw_arm) at 0.4 over the crouched carry, so the haft stays up (25-31 deg) on the forward-bent torso with the head 0.17 m from the face (THROW2 review: at 1.0 / 0.5 over the full guard arm it came to 7 cm from the nose)

runtime_clips.why: These graph leaves take their clip from a runtime callback (+0x0C), so the clip is supplied by gameplay code. Candidates were found by reverse lookup of overlay remaps (evidence listed per clip in the output).

bow.why: state-keyed hands layer on the locomotion states (weapon-base-bow)

musket.why: clip-keyed hands layer on the locomotion clips (weapon-base-long-gun)

pistol.why: no hands layer on pistol locomotion; the weapon-out finger state idle-pistol-out-part resolves 1p-idle-fingers -> pistol-right-hand-run -> actor_b-r-hand-gun -> (revolver, 2nd pass) actor_b-r-hand-revolver

spear.why: state-keyed brick-fingers hands layer (weapon-base-pick-up) on every state: the throwing grip p-fingers-brick

tomahawk.why: THROW2: the knife grip pose (carry_overrides.poses.knife_grip, the first frame of atk-actor_b-knife-v-thug-hit1-intro), which replaces the brick fingers on the lower-body roles; the aim poses keep the brick fingers

missing_notes.turn_l_180: idle-turn-l-180 has no Actor_B remap in any selected overlay; quick-turn-180-r resolves to actor_b-p-stealth-idle-turn-180 (direction-less substitute candidate).
missing_notes.turn_l: sprint mode has no idle-turn remap (the stand modes resolve relax-idle-turn-90-*).
missing_notes.pre_fall: pre-fall's leaf #4fff6a5b has no remap and no Actor_A or Actor_B clip; the pre-fall -> fall fade (0.5) is kept.
missing_notes.nock: the one-shot reload state resolves to bolt-rifle--reload--arms (musket) / 1p-reload--part (pistol): no Actor_B action. Firearms use the staged reload chain.
missing_notes.land_jump_run_hard: jump-long-land-run-hard's leaf land-hard^run-stumble has no remap and no Actor_B clip; landing.fallback plays land_jump_run (jump-long-land-run, same two exit records) in its place.

override_no_transition_anims.why: Skip start, stop and quick-reversal clips (the graph's own use_transition_anims = false branch): snappier response.

override_fast_hemisphere_fade.why: 0.3 s hemisphere crossfade instead of the graph's 0.75 s: less lag on strafe reversals.

override_no_idle_turns.why: Body yaw follows the camera with no turn-in-place clips.

override_immediate_land_move.why: Movement input interrupts a landing at once instead of after the graph's m2 >= 10 gate.

override_fast_aim_to_move.why: 0.3 s from aim idle into aimed movement instead of the graph's 0.5 s.

override_crouch_crossfade.why: Plain 0.25 s stand/crouch crossfade without the graph's full-body crouch-change state (substitute clip) and without its crouch-change additive layer.

override_fall_fade.why: 0.3 s into the fall loop instead of pre-fall's 0.5 s fade (the pre-fall clip itself is missing).

override_exact_hands_grip.why: Drive finger/palm/prop bones from the grip clip (grips.<w>: carry, aim_stand, aim_crouch) at weight 1 in every carry and aim pose (runtime H node), replacing the graph's hands layers (e.g. 0.9 on musket locomotion), the move-set finger layers and the weapon-out finger partial, so the weapon always sits exactly in the authored grip.

override_throw_windup_raise.why: Frontier-only wind-up for the thrown weapons: while one winds up, the graph's raise clip (throw-object-aim, 1h-aim-throw^aim) plays on the upper body seeked by Weapon.charge_amount(), so the arm draws back into the cocked aim pose as power builds, and hands over to the aim tree at full charge over throw-object-aim^aim's 0.2 s; a throw released while moving before the raise has finished plays the rest of it first (throw_raise_from_aimrun, then throw_raise_to_start). The graph has no charge field: its aim-in is the aim-idle crossfade (the aim tree weighted by Weapon.aim, the default), and it plays this raise only from aim-run.

throw_from_aimrun.when: request throw with the arm cocked

ground_to_takeoff.why: run-jump-long has no incoming record (code-driven); the takeoff clip lasts 0.1 s

crouch_to_takeoff.from: grounded states on a crouch-stance input (crouch idle, crouch move, crouch landings)
crouch_to_takeoff.why: Frontier-only: the player stands up into a jump from a crouch and the graph has no crouched jump; with ground_to_takeoff's 0.1 s the crouch pose and the musket's crouch arms swung into the take-off at up to 27 rad/s beyond the clips' own motion (test_continuity). The take-off -> jump join then fades over the rest of this fade (fade guard)

ground_to_fall.when: airborne without a jump for longer than coyote_s
ground_to_fall.row_use_why: the record's phase >= 0.02 gate belongs to the pre-fall state itself (thresholds.prefall_exit_phase), not to the grounded source states
ground_to_fall.why: the graph enters pre-fall (code-driven) and leaves it at phase >= 0.02 with a 0.5 s fade; the pre-fall clip #4fff6a5b is missing, so the runtime fades from the grounded state straight into fall with pre-fall's 0.5 s and no phase gate

air_to_land.why: the landings' only incoming records are jump-long's 0.1 s idle request (jump_to_land_idle) and the out-of-scope wall-jump-fail-45 / -90 fall requests into fall-land-soft-idle (also 0.1 s); the landing kind is chosen by the landing rule

jump_to_fall.why: jump-long has only the idle-request exit

land_to_move.when: moving (change-move-mode with loco_enabled and move_speed > 0, or the move requests run-fw / #e2d6c492); START when use_transition_anims; fw if |dir| <= 90. Per landing (graph_variants[].use): fall landings (soft, medium, hard) after the m2 >= 10 frames gate with 0.2 s, the jump landings (jump-long-land-idle and -med) at once (phase >= 0) with 0.4 s, the damage landing after phase 0.3 and the death landing after phase 0.8 with 0.4 s
land_to_move.why: row use = the soft fall landing's record; the other landings' records differ (jump: no frame gate, 0.4 s; damage / death: phase gates, 0.4 s), so read each landing's values from graph_variants[].use

land_idle_exit.when: phase >= soft 0.6 / medium 0.8 / hard 0.8 / jump 0.9 / jump-med 0.9 / damage 0.8 / death 0.8 (fade 0.2 / 0.2 / 0.2 / 0.4 / 0.4 / 0.4 / 0.4; per landing in graph_variants[].use)

land_run_exit.when: phase >= 1.0 into run-fw, or into run-bkwd from the backward run landings (0x0002dee0); jump-long-land-run(-hard) exit at 0.9 (their first-match 1.0 record never fires first); per landing in graph_variants[].use

land_run_early_exit.when: after the m2 >= 10 gate: forward run landings -> run-fw when move_dir leaves +-45 deg; backward run landings -> run-bkwd when move_dir is within 90..135 or -135..-90 deg (leaves the straight-back cone); secondary variable = move direction (INFERRED)

land_run_stop.when: not moving (request idle), after the m2 >= 10 gate; STOP when use_transition_anims: run-fw^idle (0.2 s) from the forward run landings, run-bk^idle (0.3 s) from the backward ones; else IDLE (0.2 s / 0.3 s)

land_run_to_move.when: after the m2 >= 10 gate. Forward run landings: change-move-mode while moving (fw -> run-fw; bw -> START bw when use_transition_anims, else MOVE bw), or the backward request #e2d6c492 (0.3 s). Backward run landings (*-run-bw): change-move-mode while moving (bw -> run-bkwd; fw -> START fw when use_transition_anims, else MOVE fw), or the forward request run-fw (0.2 s)

land_crouch_change.when: change-move-mode while crouch_change_pending (crouch toggled during a landing). Fall run landings -> run-fw 0.5 s, backward run landings -> run-bkwd 0.2 s, fall idle landings -> idle 0.5 s, each after the m2 >= 10 frames gate (the fall idle landings' condition 0x00045c30 carries flags word 0x00000001; its value 10 is read as frames like every first condition above 1, graph_understanding correction 9); jump idle landings at once (phase >= 0), damage after phase 0.3 and death after phase 0.8, 0.5 s

hit_mode_change.when: change-move-mode (mode or crouch change) after the 20-frame gate (~0.667 s, frames INFERRED)

idle_to_start.when: loco_enabled and moving and use_transition_anims; fw if |dir| <= 90

idle_to_move.when: loco_enabled and moving (use_transition_anims false); fw if |dir| <= 90

move_to_aimidle.why: aim-run -> aim-idle record: MOVE with the masked aim tree stands in for aim-run (aim-walk clips move at ~0.545 m/s)

stop_mode_change.when: change-move-mode while crouch_change_pending: first match 0.2 s into crouch-change-idle^idle (flags 0x280); fallback 0.7 s into IDLE (flags 0x80) when options.crouch_change_full_body is off
stop_mode_change.why: every crouch-toggle record into crouch-change-idle^idle carries flags bit 0x200 and is followed by a fallback record for the same request; the fallback is used only when the full-body crouch-change state is off (bit 0x200 as 'target available' is INFERRED)

move_reversal.when: code request #96646cbc (fw->bw) / #e78e5cf7 (bw->fw); request names are unhashed
move_reversal.why: graph request records; the trigger (when the code sends the request) is not in the data. Proposed trigger for WP10: use_transition_anims, speed above walk and the stick reversing across the hemisphere boundary

turn_180.why: the 180 turn clips are missing for Actor_B (turn_l_180 / turn_r_180 roles), so the runtime cannot enter this state without a substitute

aimidle_to_move.why: aim-idle -> aim-run records; MOVE with the masked aim tree stands in for aim-run

idle_to_aimidle.why: no incoming record into aim-idle from locomotion; all 38 'aim' request records use 0.2

aimidle_change.when: change-move-mode (weapon or stance change); 0.5 when aim_flag_140

aimwalk_to_idle.when: request idle (first record wins; the 0.2 s duplicate is unreachable under first-match)

aimwalk_mode_change.when: change-move-mode self re-entry: 0.5 s when aim_flag_140, else 0.25 s

idle_stance_change.when: crouch toggled (change-move-mode while crouch_change_pending): first match 0.2 s into crouch-change-idle^idle, plus the crouch-change additive (crouch_change.add); fallback (options.crouch_change_full_body off): 0.5 s self re-entry into IDLE(s')
idle_stance_change.why: graph first match on a crouch toggle is the crouch_change_pending record (flags 0x280) into the full-body state crouch-change-idle^idle; its clip has no Actor_B action and plays the substitute crouch_change.<w>/<dir>.full (status substitute; options.crouch_change_full_body, default on). The unconditional re-entry records are the fallback when that option is off

crouch_change_exit.when: phase >= 0.75 while moving (0x0003d180), else phase >= 1.0 (0x0003d1b0); both 0.7 s

move_mode_change_crouch.when: crouch toggled while moving (change-move-mode while crouch_change_pending): first match 0.2 s into crouch-change-idle^idle, which exits at phase >= 0.75 while moving (crouch_change_exit) and IDLE re-enters MOVE; plus the crouch-change additive. Fallback (options.crouch_change_full_body off): 0.5 s self re-entry
move_mode_change_crouch.why: graph first match is 0x0002a940 / 0x000252c0 (order 10, crouch_change_pending, flags 0x280) into crouch-change-idle^idle, whose clip has no Actor_B action and plays the substitute crouch_change.<w>/<dir>.full (options.crouch_change_full_body, default on); the unconditional re-entry 0x0002a970 / 0x000252f0 (order 11) is the fallback when that option is off

transition_state_crouch_change.when: crouch toggled (change-move-mode while crouch_change_pending), 0.2 s; fallback with options.crouch_change_full_body off: start_mode_change / reversal_mode_change
transition_state_crouch_change.why: same first-match crouch-toggle record as idle_stance_change / move_mode_change_crouch, in the start and reversal states

reversal_mode_change.when: change-move-mode: MOVE (target hemisphere) when not use_transition_anims, else self re-entry

start_mode_change.when: change-move-mode: MOVE when not use_transition_anims, else self re-entry

land_move_gate.graph_condition: first condition >= 10.0 (value > 1, so frames; flags words 0x00010001 and, on the fall idle landings' crouch toggle, 0x00000001: graph_understanding correction 9, the flags word does not select the unit)

landing.why: The only records into a landing are jump-long's idle request (jump-long-land-idle) and the out-of-scope wall-jump-fail-45 / -90 fall requests (fall-land-soft-idle); every other landing has no incoming record, so the game code picks the landing and the rule is proposed. Band by vertical impact speed: soft < medium_impact_mps (about a 1.8 m drop) <= medium < hard_impact_mps (about 3.3 m) <= hard. Direction at touchdown: idle when not moving, run when moving with |move_dir_deg| <= thresholds.hemi_enter_deg, run_bw when moving further back (the graph's own backward landings, which exit into run-bkwd). A jump landing (last jump within jump-long + jump_land_window_s) in the soft or medium band uses the jump-long-land states; a hard impact always uses the fall table. Frontier's flat jump lands at about 4.4 m/s, so it takes the soft jump row.

directions.idle_early: jump rows only: not moving and touchdown before jump-long reaches thresholds.jump_land_phase

select_why.jump idle: jump-long-land-idle (land-hard^idle) is the target of jump-long's only authored landing record (request idle at phase >= 0.9, jump_to_land_idle), so it is the idle jump landing whenever that record could fire. Its sibling jump-long-land-idle-med (land-med^idle, same exits) is taken when the touchdown comes before phase 0.9, a short jump onto higher ground where the authored record cannot fire (INFERRED).
select_why.jump run: jump-long-land-run (land-med^run) for the soft band, its heavier sibling jump-long-land-run-hard (land-hard^run-stumble) for the medium band, by name (INFERRED). The hard sibling has no Actor_B clip, so landing.fallback plays jump-long-land-run.
select_why.run_bw: the jump landings have no backward variant; the graph's backward landings are the fall-land-*-run-bw states, which exit into run-bkwd (0x0002dee0, 0x0002de80 / 0x0002deb0). Without them a backpedal landing would play a forward clip and exit into run-fw

never_selected.land_damage_idle: fall-land-damage-idle (land-hard-damage^idle): fall damage; Frontier has none. Exported with its exits for completeness
never_selected.land_death: fall-land-death (land-hard-damage^death): lethal fall; Frontier has none. Exported with its exits for completeness

not_exported.jump-long-land-idle-no-stumble: land-hard^idle with a single 0.3 s idle exit at phase >= 0.7 (0x0003e490) and no move exits; no incoming record and no known trigger
not_exported.jump-in-place-land: landing of the in-place jump family (jump-in-place); Frontier's jump is the running long jump (run-jump-long)
not_exported.fall-land-partial: partial-body landing (land-hard^idle) that only re-enters itself (0x00021330); no incoming record and no known trigger
not_exported.dive-jump^land: swim dive landing; out of scope

tuning_notes._about: Status and reason of every tuning value (none is a graph record): proposed = a Frontier value where the graph has no record (code-entered state, runtime mapping); approximation = stands in for graph behaviour the decoded data does not give; frontier = a Frontier-only feature the graph does not have. The report lists them (Tuning).

rate_clamp.why: clamp of the locomotion playback rate = speed / blended stride on normalized timelines (plan D9), in place of the graph's calc-new-phase-from-speed callback

rate_floor_decel.why: lowest playback rate while decelerating (plan D9 / test_rates)

mode_split_hysteresis_mps.why: hysteresis around the walk / run split sqrt(v_walk * v_run) when the mode comes from the target speed (plan D9, G3)

moving_on_wish.why: the graph's move-speed field f32@C0+120 (> 0) mapped to Frontier input: moving on above this stick magnitude (plan section 7)

moving_on_speed.why: moving on above this ground speed (m/s; plan section 7)

moving_off_speed.why: moving off below this ground speed with no stick input (m/s; plan section 7)

dir_from_velocity_above.why: the move direction (f32@C0+144) comes from the velocity above this speed, else from the stick (plan section 7)

blend_angle_rate.why: smoothing rate (1/s) of the blend move angle f32@C8+4 on the circle (plan section 7)

coyote_s.why: grounded grace before the fall state; stands in for pre-fall, whose clip #4fff6a5b is missing (plan section 11)

weapon_fade_s.why: crossfade of the carry layers, grips and aim tree on a weapon change (the graph holsters and draws instead; the aim tree's own change record 0x00038070 uses 0.25 s)

stance_fade_s.why: crossfade of the upper-body stance weights (grips, aim tree) on a crouch toggle

grip_fade_s.why: fade of the exact-grip override (override_exact_hands_grip) on and off

oneshot_fade.why: fade in / out of the action partials and their twins (draw, holster, nock, reloads): the graph's action states are entered by code with no transition record. Fade-in raised from 0.1 to 0.2 s in the WP6 review: at 0.1 s the crossfade from the carry pose into an action's first pose turned the arms at 40-58 rad/s (test_continuity storm, 26 + 12 frames)

fire_fade.why: fade in / out of the fire additives: the graph's fire state is entered by code with no transition record; the fire clip's first frame is already the recoil

hit_add_fade.why: fade in / out of the light-hit additive (hit-reaction-par is entered by code; its exit record 0x000323b0 cuts at phase 0.9 with fade 0, so the fade-out ends by then)

charge_fire_fade.why: fade of the bow's fire additives: the held draw (a Frontier-only layer) hands over to the fire clip during its fade-in (bow-fire--add at 0 is 0.7 rad from the held draw at the drawing shoulder, 2.2 rad from the bind pose)

charge_let_down_s.why: a let-down (the draw drops without a shot) unwinds the Frontier-only held-draw layer over this long instead of in one frame

carry_join_s.why: at the graph's fade-0 lower joins (e.g. take-off -> jump, record 0x00026ab0) the base clip cuts as authored; the carry-layer stacks of the two states differ (musket take-off has no rifle-run-arms layer, the jump has) and the decoded layer records give weights only, not how the layers change at such a cut. The incoming layers ramp from the outgoing amounts over this long; PlayerAnim.strict_graph_cuts (off) cuts them with the base clip, the literal reading, which snaps the musket's left wrist at about 112 rad/s

blocked_len_m.why: chest-ray length per weapon for the graph's weapon-blocked weight C8+172 = clamp((L - hit) / (0.5 L)) (plan section 7)

blocked_smooth_s.why: smoothing of the blocked weight C8+172

pitch_smooth_s.why: critically damped filter on the aim elevation that drives the aim up / down additives C8+248 / C8+252

chest_height_fallback.why: chest height (m) for the aim elevation when the metrics table has none (measured values come from actor_b_clip_metrics.json)

upper_suppress_fade_s.why: the upper aim weight fades to 0 in / back from a heavy hit or death over these times (plan G4)

aim_stance_on.why: Weapon.aim above which the lower body takes the aim-idle stance (plan risk 14)

aim_walk_max_speed_mps.why: target-speed limit of the optional aim-walk bank (options.aim_walk, off)

throw_windup_fade_s.why: the thrown weapons' wind-up raise (Frontier-only, options.throw_windup_raise; off by default, on only through gameplay_overrides.override_throw_windup_raise): the raise clip throw-object-aim, seeked by Weapon.charge_amount() like the bow's held draw, fades in over this long and hands over to the aim tree at full charge over the graph's throw-object-aim^aim -> aim-idle fade

throw_release_timeout_s.why: Throwable.anim_release_timeout while the animation drives the release (Throwable.wait_for_anim_release): the weapon's timer fallback past release_time when no release event came (the running throw's raise remainder delays the event)

options_notes.use_transition_anims: graph default: start, stop and quick-reversal states are used (i32@C0+128 truthy)
options_notes.idle_turns: graph default: idle-turn-l/r entered when idle_turn_deg leaves +-10 deg
options_notes.turn_180: graph states exist but have no Actor_B clip; no-op until a substitute is chosen
options_notes.holster: graph default: holster plays the draw clip backwards (start phase 1.0, negative rate)
options_notes.crouch_change_add: graph default: the crouch-change additive state (#8390fa57 -> actor_b-p-stand^crouch-<weapon>--add) plays on a crouch toggle
options_notes.crouch_change_full_body: graph default (on): a crouch toggle takes the graph's first-match record into the full-body state crouch-change-idle^idle (0.2 s) from every locomotion state. Its resolved clip (stand^crouch / crouch^stand) has no Actor_B action, so it plays the Actor_B full-body pair actor_b-p-stand^crouch--base / actor_b-p-crouch^stand--base (status substitute; same 1.0 s family as the resolved crouch-change additives). Off: the rows' fallback records (change-move-mode self re-entry, 0.5 s) plus the additive, the only path that needs no substitute clip
options_notes.weapon_out_fingers: graph default (on): the code-entered weapon-out finger state idle-pistol-out-part plays hand_states.<w>/<stance>.weapon_out as a looping partial at weight 1 over the lower-body layers whenever a weapon is out (weapon_layers.order step 3; weight and trigger INFERRED), for the weapons whose weapon-base set remaps its leaf (musket, pistol; not the bow, see weapon_layers.weapon_out.apply_rule). It is the only graph source of the pistol's r_hand_prop_attachment on locomotion
options_notes.aim_walk: off by user requirement: the graph's aim-run clips travel ~0.545 m/s, so aimed movement uses the masked aim tree over locomotion plus AimStabilizer (feet stay planted); enable only for steady aim below tuning.aim_walk_max_speed_mps
options_notes.pistol_sub_type: revolver (staged reload, revolver grip); pistol-actor_b is the alternative sub-type
options_notes.throw_windup_raise: graph default (off): a thrown weapon's wind-up is the graph's aim-in, the aim-idle crossfade: the aim tree (1h-aim-throw-idle, the cocked pose, with its pitch additives) weighted by Weapon.aim like every other weapon's raise; a throw is then entered from aim-idle / aim-run with request throw (throw_from_aimidle 0x00037fb0, throw_from_aimrun 0x00030930). On only through gameplay_overrides.override_throw_windup_raise (Frontier-only): the raise clip throw-object-aim (1h-aim-throw^aim), which the graph plays only from aim-run, seeked by the wind-up charge
